DatasetCollection

DatasetCollection.Rd

A DatasetCollection object represents the metadata of a Synapse Dataset Collection. https://rest-docs.synapse.org/rest/org/sagebionetworks/repo/model/table/DatasetCollection.html

A Dataset Collection is a type of view defined by a flat list of Datasets.

Usage

DatasetCollection(id=NULL, name=NULL, parent_id=NULL, activity=NULL, version_number=NULL, view_entity_type="datasetcollection", view_type_mask=256L, include_default_columns=TRUE, description=NULL, etag=NULL, created_on=NULL, modified_on=NULL, created_by=NULL, modified_by=NULL, version_label=NULL, version_comment=NULL, is_latest_version=NULL, is_search_enabled=NULL, items=list(), columns=list(), annotations=list())

Format

An S3-style class object.

Arguments

id

(Optional[character]) The unique immutable ID for this dataset collection. A new ID will be generated for new DatasetCollections. Once issued, this ID is guaranteed to never change or be re-issued

name

(Optional[character]) The name of this dataset collection. Must be 256 characters or less. Names may only contain: letters, numbers, spaces, underscores, hyphens, periods, plus signs, apostrophes, and parentheses

parent_id

(Optional[character]) The ID of the Entity that is the parent of this dataset collection.

activity

(Optional[Activity]) The Activity model represents the main record of Provenance in Synapse. It is analogous to the Activity defined in the W3C Specification on Provenance.

version_number

(Optional[integer]) The version number issued to this version on the object.

view_entity_type

(character) The API model string for the type of view. This is used to determine the default columns that are added to the table. Defaults to "datasetcollection".

view_type_mask

(integer) The Bit Mask representing DatasetCollection type. As defined in the Synapse REST API: https://rest-docs.synapse.org/rest/GET/column/tableview/defaults.html. Defaults to 256.

include_default_columns

(Optional[logical]) When creating a dataset collection or view, specifies if default columns should be included. Default columns are columns that are automatically added to the dataset collection or view. These columns are managed by Synapse and cannot be modified. If you attempt to create a column with the same name as a default column, you will receive a warning when you store the dataset collection.

include_default_columns is only used if this is the first time that the view is being stored. If you are updating an existing view this attribute will be ignored.

The column you are overriding will not behave the same as a default column. For example, suppose you create a column called id on a DatasetCollection. When using a default column, the id stores the Synapse ID of each of the entities included in the scope of the view. If you override the id column with a new column, the id column will no longer store the Synapse ID of the entities in the view. Instead, it will store the values you provide when you store the dataset collection. It will be stored as an annotation on the entity for the row you are modifying.

description

(Optional[character]) The description of the dataset collection. Must be 1000 characters or less.

etag

(Optional[character]) Synapse employs an Optimistic Concurrency Control (OCC) scheme to handle concurrent updates. Since the E-Tag changes every time an entity is updated it is used to detect when a client's current representation of an entity is out-of-date.

created_on

(Optional[character]) The date this dataset collection was created.

modified_on

(Optional[character]) The date this dataset collection was last modified. In YYYY-MM-DD-Thh:mm:ss.sssZ format

created_by

(Optional[character]) The ID of the user that created this dataset collection.

modified_by

(Optional[character]) The ID of the user that last modified this dataset collection.

version_label

(Optional[character]) The version label for this dataset collection.

version_comment

(Optional[character]) The version comment for this dataset collection.

is_latest_version

(Optional[logical]) If this is the latest version of the object.

is_search_enabled

(Optional[logical]) When creating or updating a dataset collection or view specifies if full text search should be enabled. Note that enabling full text search might slow down the indexing of the dataset collection or view.

items

(Optional[list[EntityRef]]) The flat list of datasets that define this collection. This is effectively a list of the rows that are in/will be in the collection after it is stored. The only way to add or remove rows is to add or remove items from this list.

columns

(Optional[Union[list[Column], OrderedDict[str, Column], dict[str, Column]]]) The columns of this dataset collection. This is an ordered named list where the key is the name of the column and the value is the Column object. When creating a new instance of a DatasetCollection object you may pass any of the following types as the columns argument:

- A list of Column objects
- A named list where the key is the name of the column and the value is the Column object

The order of the columns will be the order they are stored in Synapse. If you need to reorder the columns the recommended approach is to use the synReorderColumn() function. Additionally, you may add, and delete columns using the synAddColumn(), and synDeleteColumn() functions on your dataset collection class instance.

You may modify the attributes of the Column object to change the column type, name, or other attributes. For example, suppose you'd like to change a column from a INTEGER to a DOUBLE. You can do so by changing the column type attribute of the Column object. The next time you store the dataset collection the column will be updated in Synapse with the new type.


library(synapser)
synLogin()

collection = DatasetCollection(id = "syn1234") |> synGet()
collection$columns[["my_column"]]$column_type = "DOUBLE"
collection = collection |> synStore()



Note that the keys in this named list should match the column names as they are in Synapse. However, know that the name attribute of the Column object is used for all interactions with the Synapse API. The named list key is purely for the usage of this interface. For example, if you wish to rename a column you may do so by changing the name attribute of the Column object. The key in the named list does not need to be changed. The next time you store the dataset collection the column will be updated in Synapse with the new name and the key in the named list will be updated.

annotations

(Optional[dict[str, Union[list[str], list[bool], list[float], list[int], list[date], list[datetime]]]]) Additional metadata associated with the dataset collection. The key is the name of your desired annotations. The value is an object containing a list of values (use empty list to represent no values for key) and the value type associated with all values in the list.

Value

NULL

Methods

  • DatasetCollection(id=NULL, name=NULL, parent_id=NULL, activity=NULL, version_number=NULL, view_entity_type="datasetcollection", view_type_mask=256L, include_default_columns=TRUE, description=NULL, etag=NULL, created_on=NULL, modified_on=NULL, created_by=NULL, modified_by=NULL, version_label=NULL, version_comment=NULL, is_latest_version=NULL, is_search_enabled=NULL, items=list(), columns=list(), annotations=list()): Constructor for DatasetCollection

  • synAddColumn(instance, column, index=NULL): Add column(s) to the table. Note that this does not store the column(s) in Synapse. You must call the synStore() function on this DatasetCollection instance to store the column(s) in Synapse. This is a convenience function to eliminate the need to manually add the column(s) to the $columns list.

    This function will add an item to the $columns attribute of the DatasetCollection instance. $columns is a named list where the key is the name of the column and the value is the Column object.

  • synAddItem(instance, item): Adds a dataset to the dataset collection. Effect is not seen until the dataset collection is stored.

  • synDeleteColumn(instance, name): Mark a column for deletion. Note that this does not delete the column from Synapse. You must call the synStore() function on this DatasetCollection instance to delete the column from Synapse. This is a convenience function to eliminate the need to manually delete the column from the named list and add it to the $_columns_to_delete attribute.

  • synDeletePermissions(instance, include_self=TRUE, include_container_content=FALSE, recursive=FALSE, target_entity_types=NULL, dry_run=FALSE, show_acl_details=TRUE, show_files_in_containers=TRUE, synapse_client=NULL): Delete the entire Access Control List (ACL) for a given Entity. This is not scoped to a specific user or group, but rather removes all permissions associated with the Entity. After this operation, the Entity will inherit permissions from its benefactor, which is typically its parent entity or the Project it belongs to.

    In order to remove permissions for a specific user or group, you should use the synSetPermissions() function with the access_type set to an empty list.

    By default, Entities such as FileEntity and Folder inherit their permission from their containing Project. For such Entities the Project is the Entity's 'benefactor'. This permission inheritance can be overridden by creating an ACL for the Entity. When this occurs the Entity becomes its own benefactor and all permission are determined by its own ACL.

    If the ACL of an Entity is deleted, then its benefactor will automatically be set to its parent's benefactor.

    Special notice for Projects: The ACL for a Project cannot be deleted, you must individually update or revoke the permissions for each user or group.

  • synGetAcl(instance, principal_id=NULL, check_benefactor=TRUE, synapse_client=NULL): Get the ACL that a user or group has on an Entity.

  • synGetPermissions(instance, synapse_client=NULL): Get the permissions that the caller has on an Entity.

  • synListAcl(instance, recursive=FALSE, include_container_content=FALSE, target_entity_types=NULL, log_tree=FALSE, synapse_client=NULL): List the Access Control Lists (ACLs) for this entity and optionally its children.

    This function returns the local sharing settings for the entity and optionally its children. It provides a mapping of all ACLs for the given container/entity.

    Important Note: This function returns the LOCAL sharing settings only, not the effective permissions that each Synapse User ID/Team has on the entities. More permissive permissions could be granted via a Team that the user has access to that has permissions on the entity, or through inheritance from parent entities.

  • synQuery(query, include_row_id_and_row_version=TRUE, convert_to_datetime=FALSE, download_location=NULL, quote_character="\"", escape_character=r"(\)", line_end="\n", separator=",", header=TRUE, timeout=250L, synapse_client=NULL): Query for data on a table stored in Synapse. The results will always be returned as a data frame unless you specify a download_location in which case the results will be downloaded to that location. There are a number of arguments that you may pass to this function depending on if you are getting the results back as a data frame or downloading the results to a file.

  • synQueryPartMask(query, part_mask, timeout=250L, synapse_client=NULL): Query for data on a table stored in Synapse. This is a more advanced use case of the synQuery() function that allows you to determine what additional metadata about the table or query should also be returned. If you do not need this additional information then you are better off using the synQuery() function.

    The query for this method uses this Rest API: https://rest-docs.synapse.org/rest/POST/entity/id/table/query/async/start.html

  • synRemoveItem(instance, item): Removes an entity from the dataset collection. Must be a Dataset or EntityRef. Effect is not seen until the dataset collection is stored. Unless the version is specified, all entities with the same ID will be removed.

  • synReorderColumn(instance, name, index): Reorder a column in the table. Note that this does not store the column in Synapse. You must call the synStore() function on this DatasetCollection instance to store the column in Synapse. This is a convenience function to eliminate the need to manually reorder the named list stored in the $columns attribute.

    You must ensure that the index is within the bounds of the number of columns in the table. If you pass in an index that is out of bounds the column will be added to the end of the list.

  • synSetPermissions(instance, principal_id=NULL, access_type=NULL, modify_benefactor=FALSE, warn_if_inherits=TRUE, overwrite=TRUE, synapse_client=NULL): Sets permission that a user or group has on an Entity. An Entity may have its own ACL or inherit its ACL from a benefactor.

  • synSnapshot(instance, comment=NULL, label=NULL, include_activity=TRUE, associate_activity_to_new_version=TRUE, timeout=120L, synapse_client=NULL): Creates a snapshot of the dataset collection. A snapshot is a saved, read-only version of the dataset collection at the time it was created. Dataset collection snapshots are created using the asynchronous job API.

  • synUpdateRows(instance, values, primary_keys, dry_run=FALSE, rows_per_query=50000L, update_size_bytes=1992294.4, insert_size_bytes=943718400L, job_timeout=600L, date_columns=NULL, date_format=NULL, wait_for_eventually_consistent_view=FALSE, wait_for_eventually_consistent_view_timeout=600L, synapse_client=NULL): Update the values of rows in the dataset collection. This method can only be used to update values in custom columns. Default columns cannot be updated, but may be used as primary keys.

    Limitations:

    - When updating many rows the requests to Synapse will be chunked into smaller requests. The limit is 2MB per request. This chunking will happen automatically and should not be a concern for most users. If you are having issues with the request being too large you may lower the number of rows you are trying to update.
    - The primary_keys argument must contain at least one column.
    - The primary_keys argument cannot contain columns that are a LIST type.
    - The primary_keys argument cannot contain columns that are a JSON type.
    - The values used as the primary_keys must be unique in the table. If there are multiple rows with the same values in the primary_keys the behavior is that an error will be raised.
    - The columns used in primary_keys cannot contain updated values. Since the values in these columns are used to determine if a row exists, they cannot be updated in the same transaction.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## Example 1: Create a new Dataset Collection from a list of Datasets.
    library(synapser)
    synLogin()

    my_datasets = list(Dataset(id = "syn1234"), Dataset(id = "syn1235"), Dataset(id = "syn1236"))
    my_collection = DatasetCollection(parent_id = "syn987", name = "my-new-collection", items = my_datasets)
    my_collection |> synStore()

## Example 2: Add Datasets to an existing Dataset Collection.
    library(synapser)
    synLogin()

    my_collection = DatasetCollection(id = "syn1234") |> synGet()

    # Add a dataset to the collection
    my_collection |> synAddItem(Dataset(id = "syn1235"))
    my_collection |> synStore()

## Example 3: Remove Datasets from a Dataset Collection.
    library(synapser)
    synLogin()

    my_collection = DatasetCollection(id = "syn1234") |> synGet()

    # Remove a dataset from the collection
    my_collection |> synRemoveItem(Dataset(id = "syn1235"))
    my_collection |> synStore()

## Example 4: Query data from a Dataset Collection.
    library(synapser)
    synLogin()

    row = synQuery(query = "SELECT * FROM syn1234 WHERE id = 'syn1235'")
    print(row)

## Example 5: Add a custom column to a Dataset Collection.
    library(synapser)
    synLogin()

    my_collection = DatasetCollection(id = "syn1234") |> synGet()
    my_collection |> synAddColumn(Column(name = "my_annotation", column_type = "STRING"))
    my_collection |> synStore()

## Example 6: Update custom column values in a Dataset Collection.
    library(synapser)
    synLogin()

    my_collection = DatasetCollection(id = "syn1234") |> synGet()
    # my_annotation must already exist in the dataset collection as a custom column
    modified_data = data.frame(
        id = c("syn1234"),
        my_annotation = c("good data")
    )
    my_collection |> synUpdateRows(values = modified_data, primary_keys = list("id"), dry_run = FALSE)

## Example 7: Save a snapshot of a Dataset Collection.
    library(synapser)
    synLogin()

    my_collection = DatasetCollection(id = "syn1234") |> synGet()
    my_collection |> synSnapshot(comment = "My first snapshot", label = "My first snapshot")

## Example 8: Deleting a Dataset Collection.
    library(synapser)
    synLogin()

    DatasetCollection(id = "syn4567") |> synDelete()
} # }
